text: Take all integers between 20 and 45, including both endpoints. First, keep only the numbers that are strictly less than 30. Next, replace each remaining number with its remainder modulo 19, taken in the range 0 to 18. Finally, report the average of the remaining numbers rounded to an integer, rounding halves to the even neighbour.

Consider the integers from 15 to 32, inclusive. First, retain only the even integers. Next, replace each remaining number with the sum of its decimal digits (ignoring any minus sign). Of these numbers, count how many of the remaining values are equal to zero.

Start with the inclusive integer range [21, 33]. First, retain only the values whose decimal representation includes the digit 2. Then, scale every remaining value by a factor of 3. Finally, report the minimum of the remaining values.

Consider the integers from 1 to 50, inclusive. First, discard every number that is 33 or smaller. Then, map every remaining value to the digit sum of its absolute value. Then, replace each remaining number x with x * x. Then, replace each remaining number with its remainder modulo 8, taken in the range 0 to 7. Of these numbers, give the mode of the remaining numbers, choosing the smallest value in case of a tie.
Consider the integers from 15 to 195, inclusive. First, discard every number that is 80 or greater. Finally, find the least value among the remaining numbers.

Start with the inclusive integer range [35, 143]. First, discard every number that is 70 or smaller. Then, scale every remaining value by a factor of 2. Of these numbers, find the greatest value among the remaining numbers.

Take all integers between 20 and 103, including both endpoints. First, keep only the perfect squares. Then, decrease every remaining value by 6. Next, replace each remaining number x with x mod 20, where the result lies in 0 to 19. Of these numbers, count how many values remain.
